body.v: The password for your ThisIsTea account was just changed. If you did this, there is nothing more to do.
If you changed it because you typed your old one into a page you did not trust, tell your IT or security team too, and turn on multi-factor authentication under Security in the app.

hotspots.explain: The address is on thisistea.example, the real domain.
A calm confirmation. It does not threaten you or set a deadline.
No link to click. It sends you to the app you already have.
Multi-factor authentication is the second lock: a stolen password alone no longer opens the door.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: ThisIsTea itself: the address is on thisistea.example.
choices: A scammer using a lookalike address

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: None. It is a calm confirmation after you changed your password yourself.
choices: None: it is a calm confirmation

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Nothing urgent. It only suggests telling IT and turning on multi-factor authentication if you were tricked.
choices: Click a link and sign in
Nothing, apart from good habits if you were tricked

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: You have already done the right thing. If you clicked and typed your password earlier, change it from the real site, tell IT straight away and turn on multi-factor authentication. Speed is the whole game.
choices: Delete the email and say nothing
Wait a few days to see what happens
Change it from the real site, tell IT and add a second lock

actions.label: Change the password from the real site and turn on multi-factor authentication
actions.consequence: One stolen password is now a scratch, not a crack in the shell.

actions.label: Report it to IT straight away
actions.consequence: Your report may protect the colleague who got the same email.

actions.label: Delete the email and say nothing: if nobody noticed, no harm done
actions.consequence: Staying quiet only gives the attacker time. The colleague next to you may get the same email.

actions.label: Wait a few days to see whether anything strange happens
actions.consequence: Waiting gives the attacker time to use your login.

attacker_reveal: This one is real, dear, and it is exactly what a real service does after a password change. If you were tricked earlier, this is the moment for the plan: change the password, add a second lock and tell IT. Waiting or staying quiet only helps the trickster.
